correctness.rationale: Exhaustively generated the thirty-edge icosahedral matching complex (face counts 30,315,1400,2535,1482,125); checked signed boundary compositions. Exactly 2911 integral unit-pivot eliminations leave 65 degree-three cells and one degree-four cell with a nonzero integer boundary column of gcd three. Therefore reduced integral H3 is \(\mathbb Z^{64}\oplus\mathbb Z/3\) and all other reduced integral homology vanishes. The 120 automorphisms and the 60-element commutator subgroup are fully enumerated. Over F3 the antipodal even/odd H4 dimensions are 0/1 (chain dimensions 741 each, boundary ranks 686/55 and 670/70), so natural universal coefficients force inversion to negate torsion. Over F5 exact H3 eigenspace dimensions are 40/24 and equal the rational ones; the full torsion representation factors through the quotient C2, nontrivial on inversion. The included standalone exact verifier was executed successfully on its supplied path.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General torsion existence for complete-graph or chessboard matching complexes does not transfer this particular antipodal sign, even though the icosahedral matching complex is a subcomplex of the complete-graph matching complex. The line-graph claw-free theorem bounds connectivity, with no equivariant torsion information. The outerplanar theorem neither includes the icosahedron (thirty edges versus an outerplanar twelve-vertex edge bound of twenty-one) nor computes group actions.

value.rationale: The uniquely occurring order-three torsion of this canonical planar icosahedral matching complex is a naturally motivated invariant after the established non-sphere-wedge result. Its action under the canonical antipode is genuinely undetermined by the underlying Moore-space summand, and the negative result gives the full torsion character and a nonexistence of globally invariant order-three class. The associated 40/24 rational parity split reveals distinct free/torsion symmetry behavior; both are natural equivariant homology data with potential use in quotient and symmetry-sensitive topology. The claim is not a generic substitution, a normalization convention, or a recomputation of an ordinary Betti number.
